surprises.description: Q4 guidance was stronger than the preview’s bar: revenue is guided to $352–360 million, with a $356 million midpoint near the top of the preview’s estimated $350–356 million range, and EPS guidance of $0.62–$0.70 is above the $0.60 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 guidance projects revenue of $352–360 million” and “EPS of $0.62–0.70,” with two fewer billing days than Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4'26 consensus EPS $0.60” and applying Q4 seasonality implies a “~$350–356M Q4 bar”; the base scenario expected revenue of “~$348–358M” and EPS of “$0.57–0.65.”

surprises.description: Technology revenue growth reached 7.8% year over year, ahead of the preview’s implied expectation of about 6.8% and clearing its 6% threshold for sustaining the acceleration narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: Technology revenue grew “7.8% YoY and 2.5% sequentially on a billing day basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Technology growth of “~+6.8% YoY” and said “below +6%” would stall the acceleration narrative.

surprises.description: Flex gross margins improved 60 basis points year over year, stronger than the preview’s expectation that Flex margin would be around 26.7–26.9% or ease seasonally. The overall gross margin, by contrast, matched the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Flex gross margins improving 60 basis points,” reflecting “strong pricing discipline and a richer business mix”; overall gross margin was 28.2%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put Flex gross margin at “~26.8%,” with a “26.7–26.9%” range, and said the base case could see it “easing ~10 bps seasonally”; it estimated overall gross margin at “~28.2%.”

surprises.description: The EPS headline was boosted by an unexpected $0.12 one-time insurance gain: reported EPS of $0.90 was well above the $0.76 consensus, while EPS excluding the gain was about $0.78—only slightly above consensus and near the high end of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EPS was $0.90,” including “a $0.12 one-time gain from corporate-owned life insurance policies”; excluding it, EPS was “near the high end of guidance” and up approximately 24% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus EPS of “$0.76” and company guidance of “$0.71–$0.79.”

surprises.description: Consulting Solutions showed unusually strong commercial momentum: it posted record new contract award value and converted the highest share of pipeline opportunities in its history, exceeding the preview’s base-case expectation of stability without new leading-indicator data.
surprises.fact_evidence: Consulting Solutions “achieved record new contract award value in Q3” and “converted the highest percentage of pipeline opportunities in its history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described “continued stability” without “new leading-indicator data,” while its bull case looked for double-digit job-order and start growth.

surprises.description: AI-related pipeline growth and demand breadth were stronger than the preview had specifically anticipated: AI pipelines were up about 20% year over year, while eight of ten industry sectors were stable or growing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-related pipelines are up roughly 20% year-over-year,” and “8 of 10 industry sectors are stable or growing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged AI and Consulting Solutions commentary as important, but did not specify AI pipeline growth or expect a quantified broad-sector demand update.

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was positive but fell short of expectations, rather than delivering the stronger cash-conversion inflection the preview was watching for. Management attributed the shortfall to a large client’s temporary payment delay, resolved in early October, and expected Q4 to remain cash flow positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating cash flow was “$9.5 million, below expectations due to a temporary payment delay from a large client that was resolved in early October,” with Q4 expected to remain cash flow positive.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for an “Operating cash flow inflection” and a “reversal of the H1 working-capital drag,” and identified another quarter of negative FCF as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: The average technology bill rate rose to $91 per hour and expanded for a second consecutive quarter, a stronger pricing indicator than the preview’s emphasis on merely holding bill-pay spreads.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average technology bill rate rose to $91 per hour, expanding for the second consecutive quarter” due to higher-margin consulting engagements and disciplined wage management.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “continued stability in bill-pay spreads,” while its bull case called for pricing to hold.

surprises.description: Total Q3 revenue exceeded both the consensus estimate and the high end of company guidance, though the dollar gap was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue was “$357.8 million,” exceeding the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited consensus revenue of “$354.4M” and guidance of “$349–357M.”
